title: Accessing childes-db
text: childesr package allows access data childes-db R. removes need write complex SQL queries order get information want database. vignette shows examples use data loading functions resulting data look like. several different get_ functions can use extract different types data childes-db: get_transcripts() get_participants() get_tokens() get_types() get_utterances() get_speaker_statistics() get_sql_query() Technical note 1: childesr 0.3, data retrieved versioned childes-db dataset Redivis (using redivis R package) rather MySQL server, database connection needed. Install redivis client install.packages("redivis", repos = "https://langcog.r-universe.dev"). (bug redivis macOS binaries built 2026-07-31 broke OAuth token caching, causing repeated browser authentication prompts; current r-universe binaries fine — see repeated auth prompts, update redivis package.) dataset public, Redivis account required; headless scripted use can authenticate API token — created workspace settings redivis.com set via Sys.setenv(REDIVIS_API_TOKEN = "...") — bypasses OAuth cache entirely. connection argument get_ functions connect_to_childes() / clear_connections() functions deprecated retained backwards compatibility. Technical note 2: tried optimize time takes get data database. try query get tokens, take long time.

title: Accessing childes-db
text: get_transcripts function returns high-level information transcripts available database. can filter query get transcripts specific collection, corpus, child. example, can run get_transcripts without arguments return transcripts database. want information specific collection, English-American transcripts, can specify collection argument. know corpus want analyze, can specify corpus argument. following function call return information transcripts Brown corpus. want one corpus, can pass multiple corpus names. can also pass one name collections child arguments. want transcript information specific child corpus, pass name child argument. Note following function call return transcripts Brown corpus child Shem present corpus.
code: d_transcripts <- get_transcripts() head(d_transcripts) ## NULL d_eng_na <- get_transcripts(collection = "Eng-NA") head(d_eng_na) ## NULL # returns all transcripts in the brown corpus d_brown_transcripts <- get_transcripts(corpus = "Brown") # print the number of rows nrow(d_brown_transcripts) ## NULL d_many_corpora <- get_transcripts(corpus = c("Brown", "Clark")) # print the number of rows nrow(d_many_corpora) ## NULL d_shem <- get_transcripts(corpus = c("Brown", "Clark"),                           target_child = "Shem") # print the number of rows nrow(d_shem) ## NULL

title: Accessing childes-db
text: get_participants function returns background information speakers (children adults) database. includes information : speaker’s role conversation language sex SES youngest age transcript oldest age transcript , run function arguments, get background information speakers database. participants function introduces three new arguments: role, age, sex. role argument allows get information specific kind speaker, “target_child.” age argument takes number indicating age(s) children (months) want analyze. can use argument two ways Pass single number information participants transcript age. Pass range ages get information participants transcript within certain age range. example, can get participant information children transcripts ages 24 36 months.
code: d_participants <- get_participants() head(d_participants) ## NULL d_target_child <- get_participants(role = "target_child") head(d_target_child) ## NULL d_age_range <- get_participants(age = c(24, 36)) head(d_age_range) ## NULL

title: Accessing childes-db
text: get_tokens function returns table row token based set filtering criteria. token argument allows pass vector one tokens want analyze. example, wanted get production data specific token(s), run following call get instances “dog” “ball” Adam Brown corpus.
code: d_adam_prod <- get_tokens(corpus = "Brown",                           role = "target_child",                           target_child = "Adam",                           token = c("dog", "ball"))  # view the structure of the data str(d_adam_prod) ##  NULL # print the unique tokens unique(d_adam_prod$gloss) ## NULL

title: Accessing childes-db
text: get_types() function works like get_tokens() function, returning table row type based set filtering criteria. type argument allows pass vector one types want analyze. main difference now single row type (.e., concept) variable count tracks number times type appeared particular transcript. example, wanted get production data specific type(s), run following call get counts “dog” “ball” Adam’s transcripts Brown corpus.
code: d_adam_types <- get_types(corpus = "Brown",                           target_child = "Adam",                           role = "target_child",                           type = c("dog", "ball"))  # print the number of times ball appears in the first transcript c(d_adam_types$gloss[1], d_adam_types$count[1]) ## NULL

title: Accessing childes-db
text: get_utterances function returns table row utterance based user-defined filtering criteria. example, following function get utterances Brown Corpus child Adam.
code: d_adam_utts <- get_utterances(corpus = "Brown",                               target_child = "Adam")  # view the structure of the data str(d_adam_utts) ##  NULL # print the first five utterances d_adam_utts$gloss[1:5] ## NULL

title: Accessing childes-db
text: get_speaker_statistics() function returns table row transcript columns contain set summary statistics transcript. summary statistics include: number utterances (num_utterances) number types (num_types) number tokens (num_tokens) number morphemes (num_morphemes) mean length utterances words (mlu_w) mean length utterances morphemes (mlu_m) example, wanted get summary statistics Adam’s production data, run following call.
code: d_adam_stats <- get_speaker_statistics(corpus = "Brown",                                        target_child = "Adam",                                        role = "target_child")  # get the average mlu across all Adam's transcripts if (!is.null(d_adam_stats)) mean(d_adam_stats$mlu_w)

title: Accessing childes-db
text: get_sql_query() function returns table SQL query run specified database version. childesr 0.3, queries run Redivis’s query engine, uses BigQuery Standard SQL rather MySQL’s dialect. example, wanted see top 10 corpora Eng-NA collection highest count token “dog”, run following call.
code: d_na_dog <- get_sql_query("SELECT corpus_name, COUNT(id) AS count FROM token WHERE collection_name = 'Eng-NA' AND gloss = 'dog' GROUP BY corpus_name")  # (the getters return NULL, with a message, if the database is unreachable) if (!is.null(d_na_dog)) dplyr::arrange(d_na_dog, desc(count))

title: childesr 0.3.0
text: data now retrieved versioned childes-db dataset Redivis (https://redivis.com/datapages/datasets/childes_db) instead MySQL server; get_ function interface outputs unchanged filtering large content tables (tokens, utterances, types) happens server-side Redivis, matching rows transferred connect_to_childes(), clear_connections(), connection db_args arguments deprecated ignored (connection needed) get_sql_query() now runs BigQuery Standard SQL (Redivis’s query engine) instead MySQL SQL get_tokens(replace = TRUE) now correctly drops replacement column; previously bug kept dropped dependencies DBI, dbplyr, RMySQL; added Suggests dependency redivis client (installable https://langcog.r-universe.dev) current database version now childes-db 2026.1 (Redivis v1.4). adds token_morpheme table (accessible via get_sql_query(); dedicated getters may follow) reworks morphological parsing, morpheme-based measures (e.g. mlu_m, num_morphemes) comparable earlier versions. always, numeric ids internal release – pin db_version reproducible analyses use pid link transcripts across versions
